questions.q: Which of these are reasons for compressing a file? Tick all that apply.
options: It takes up less storage space
It can be sent over a network more quickly
It makes the file open faster in every program
It improves the quality of the data
correct: It takes up less storage space
It can be sent over a network more quickly
questions.feedback: Smaller means less space and less time to send. Compression never improves quality — lossy compression reduces it.

questions.q: Explain why a text document must be compressed losslessly rather than lossily.

markPoints.concept: lossy compression permanently removes some of the data
markPoints.exemplar: Lossy compression permanently removes some of the data.

markPoints.concept: and every character of a document matters, so the meaning would change
accept: every character|every letter|every word|each character|meaning|unreadable|nonsense|change the meaning|changed|corrupt|not make sense|would not read
markPoints.exemplar: Every character matters, so removing any of them would change what the document says.

questions.example: Lossy compression works by permanently throwing away data that will not be noticed. In a document every character matters, so losing any of them would change what it says, which means only lossless compression can be used.
questions.paraphrase: Because the lossy method deletes information for good, and in text every single letter counts, taking some out would alter the meaning.
questions.feedback: What lossy does, then why that is unacceptable here.

options: Some of it has been permanently discarded and cannot be recovered
It has been rearranged and can be restored exactly
It has been moved into the file's metadata

questions.feedback: JPEG is lossy. Saving it again at full quality will not bring the detail back.

questions.q: A film studio is deciding how to distribute a new film: as a very large lossless file, or as a smaller lossy file. Discuss the considerations involved and recommend one.

markPoints.concept: explains what lossy compression does to the film
explains what lossless compression keeps, and what it costs in size
considers download time and bandwidth for the viewer
considers storage and distribution cost for the studio
considers what most viewers would actually notice on their screens
reaches a recommendation and gives a reason for it

questions.example: A lossy version permanently removes detail the eye is least likely to notice, which makes the file far smaller. A lossless version keeps every pixel exactly, which matters to anyone watching on a large, high-quality screen, but the file may be several times bigger. For the viewer, the lossy file downloads far faster and uses much less of a monthly data allowance, and on a phone or an ordinary television the difference in quality is hard to see. For the studio, the lossy file is cheaper to store and cheaper to serve to millions of people. I would recommend offering the lossy version as the standard download, with the lossless version available to those who want it, because that gets the film to most people quickly without taking the choice away from viewers who would notice the difference.
questions.feedback: A six-mark discussion is marked by you against the points above. The mark that separates a good answer from a list is the last one: a recommendation with a reason attached to it.

questions.q: Run-length encoding replaces AAAABBBCCCCCCC with 4A3B7C. What kind of compression is this?
options: Lossless, because the original can be rebuilt exactly
Lossy, because some letters have been removed
Lossy, because the file is smaller
Neither; it is encryption rather than compression
questions.feedback: Nothing has been lost: 4A3B7C expands back to exactly what it came from.

questions.q: Explain why run-length encoding would make the file BIGGER for the string ABCDEFG.

markPoints.concept: there are no runs of repeated characters
accept: no runs|no repeat|no repeats|not repeated|all different|nothing repeats|nothing is repeated|every character is different|none repeat|no repetition|none of the letters appear twice
markPoints.exemplar: There are no runs of repeated characters.

markPoints.concept: so a count has to be stored for every single character
markPoints.exemplar: So a count of 1 has to be stored in front of every character.

questions.example: Run-length encoding only saves space where characters repeat. In ABCDEFG nothing repeats, so the encoding has to store a count of 1 in front of every single character, which makes it twice as long.
questions.paraphrase: Since none of the letters appear twice in a row, the method ends up adding a 1 before each one and the result is longer than the original.
questions.feedback: No runs, so nothing to shorten — and the counts are pure overhead.
